language-tier-unsupported.rule: The admitted universe's selected grammars do not bear the requested relation@rung. The cause is a single named state, so nativeCause carries it and must be exactly capability-missing. Already derived and enforced by the syntax capability prerequisite; stated here so one table covers every member.

provider-unavailable.rule: Section 10 leaves this row's Cause cell empty, so a null is lawful and self-describing; where a more specific named state applies it is carried. No other cause may appear.

input-closure-incomplete.rule: The one deficiency whose cause genuinely IS a single named missing input, which is why section 10 lists twelve of them and why the three body-language-* members were added here. A null refuses: this row is exactly where a null would record an unmade disclosure.

budget-exhausted.rule: Section 10 already qualifies this row `(stage terminal)`. The stage terminal is the cause and it is a closed StageTerminal value in the same entry, so nativeCause is null by design and the terminal must actually say budget-exhausted.

confidence-floor-unmet.rule: Requirement-relative and deliberately without an entry carrier: the FLOOR lives in RequirementV2.minConfidenceMillionths and the entry carries only its own confidenceMillionths, so the entry cannot decide whether the floor was met. The comparison is the sufficiency evaluation's, and stating that limit is honest where inventing an entry-level predicate would not be.

derivation-policy-unmet.relationLaw: The OWNING law scopes this deficiency to one relation. Native section 4.7 and sufficiency_v2 apply derivationPolicy only where `rel == "types"` and the requirement asks for `declared-only`; there is no derivation policy for any other relation, so no other relation's entry can be short of one. An earlier revision checked the derivationKinds carrier ALONE, and a complete Run therefore admitted this declared deficiency on a `references` entry that merely carried the same array value (root diagnostic: references ADMIT, types ADMIT). An entry whose relation is outside this list cannot declare it.
derivation-policy-unmet.rule: Section 10's Cause cell reads `compiler-inferred present`, which is a statement about derivationKinds - a closed three-member set in this same entry - and not a NativeCause. The entry must actually carry compiler-inferred among its derivation kinds.
derivation-policy-unmet.thisIsDeclarationSupportNotAnObligation: Two different assertions, and only the first is enforced. (1) An entry that DECLARES this deficiency must be for relation `types` and must actually carry `compiler-inferred`. (2) Whether a given requirement DEMANDS the deficiency is sufficiency_v2's question against a RequirementV2, and is not derived here. `compiler-inferred` types are exact under the admitted universe and are perfectly valid under `derivationPolicy=any`; they become a deficiency only under `declared-only`. Nothing here imposes declared-only on a valid types entry, and controls hold both directions.

resolution-incomplete.rule: Section 10's Cause cell reads `the unresolved edge classes; partial/not-attempted stage`, and both halves are ResolutionCompletenessV2 fields: `state` names the stage condition and `unresolvedEdgeClasses` carries EVERY applicable class at once, already forced by RC-2 to equal the admitted unresolved-edge facts of this view. A claim of this deficiency over a `complete` or `not-applicable` resolution state is refused: that is the entry contradicting its own evidence.

external-consumers-unknown.rule: Section 10's Cause cell reads `exports-open, exports-unknown`, which are the ClosedWorldV2 exportsClosed values `open` and `unknown` in this same entry, not NativeCause members. `closed` refuses: an entry cannot claim its consumers are unknown while its own closed-world record says they are closed.

required-relation-missing.rule: A sufficiency verdict about a relation the view does NOT carry an entry for, so an entry can never be its own evidence. It has no entry carrier by construction and takes no cause. Kept admissible rather than refused because nothing in this contract states that a host may not record it, and inventing that refusal is not this correction's to make.

bodyIdentityJoin.levelSpecificationRetained: normalisationVersion names the retained level specification bytes
bodyIdentityJoin.note: At L0 the canonical payload is the raw body-span bytes, so the host recomputes it from the enclosing fact anchor: a real source join. At L1-L3 it is a versioned normalizer output the host cannot recompute, so the requirement is exact retained preimage custody plus the framed-identity check. This is custody and framing evidence; it qualifies no normalizer.
bodyIdentityJoin.anchorRule: A clones fact carries exactly one anchor: the body span the identity is over. Zero anchors would leave the claim unattached and several would make the L0 recomputation a choice, which is the arbitrary-anchor defect in another form. `anchorCardinality` here is a declared MIRROR of this relation's registry `anchorLaw` (class `body-identity`, cardinality 1), which is the single enforcing statement and is applied to every relation before any payload join runs. The join checks that the two AGREE (`RELATION_ANCHOR_LAW_DRIFT`) rather than refusing the same fault a second time under a second name.
bodyIdentityJoin.languageIdSource: the BODY's language, from the SAME selector over the SAME single anchor that produces the body dialect: the `languageVersionBinding` of the fact sourceUniverse domain registry row, where `dialect.form` is `closed-suffix-table` gives `bodyLanguageByVariant[<the variant that table selects from this anchor's path suffix, longest match wins>]`, and any other dialect form gives `bodyLanguage`. The value is always a member of that row's `bodyLanguages` and of the closed foundation `#/$defs/body-language-version` `languageId` enum {javascript, rust, typescript}.
bodyIdentityJoin.languageIdIsNotTheProviderLanguage: It is emphatically NOT the domain row's own `language` field. That field names the ENGINE that read the body, and the two differ in both live cases: a `.js` body under `native.semantic-universe.typescript.v2` is a `javascript` body, not `typescript`, and every body under `native.semantic-universe.syntax.v2` would read as `syntax`, which the closed languageId enum does not contain, so a literal implementer would mint a different clone identity for every JavaScript body and NO admissible identity at all under the syntax universe. An earlier revision of this key said `the language of the fact sourceUniverse domain registry row`, which is that wrong reading; identity-and-evidence section 3 and each domain row's own `bodyLanguageLaw` always said the derived one, and the identity-model body-identity join has always checked the derived projection. This key is now the same sentence as those two.
bodyIdentityJoin.languageVersionSource: the raw 32 bytes of SHA-256(C(body-language-version)), the closed DERIVED record at foundation/identity-schemas.v2.json#/$defs/body-language-version, rebuilt by Run closure from the universe ResolvedInputs and the admitted retained native context the universe own nativeContextId names, per that universe domain languageVersionBinding. It carries the identity of the component that INTERPRETS the body span plus the selected source dialect; it never carries a human display string, an option-synthesis version, an operational platform value, a path, or a whole per-crate map. Fixed width, because the inherited frame gives each component a u8 length.
bodyIdentityJoin.tokenStreamFraming: u32be token_count || token*, token = u16be kind_id_len || kind_id || u32be value_len || value. The closure parses the retained L1-L3 stream to prove custody and framing; it does not and must not judge the tokenisation itself.
